name: README.md
html:
skeleton — the first-loading artifact

~49 KB. The loading-shimmer surface — the ONLY animation allowed on the critical path, because it is the loading placeholder. Every other widget lazy-loads on surface mount; this one loads first and stays.

 DOM skeleton layer mounts (host gets .has-skeleton-layer)
        │
        ▼
 mountWebGpuWidget(SKELETON, canvas)
        │  artifact is `eager: true` in GPU_WIDGET_ARTIFACTS —
        │  the fetch may start before the canvas exists
        ▼
 Skeleton::init → gpu-mini pipeline + a STORAGE buffer
        │  (24 rects × 4 vec4 rows — the "sheet")
        ▼
 per frame: widget.frame(dt) → the sheet's rects morph
   glyph-zero ↔ glyph-one per cell, per-cell cadence staggered,
   density gates + row raggedness + resolve collapse

The sheet contract — why storage, not uniform

The sheet holds up to MAX_RECTS = 24 rects, 4 vec4 rows each: rect (x,y,w,h) · meta (radius, cell size, row size, unused) · sbase · sink. A uniform block caps at a few KB and is meant for per-draw constants — a per-rect data table belongs in a storage buffer, which the shader indexes by rect_index. The JS/Rust sync contract (SHEET_VEC4S = MAX_RECTS * 4) is in lib.rs; count must never exceed MAX_RECTS or the shader reads garbage rows.

Safe tuning

  • MAX_RECTS (24): max simultaneous skeleton placeholders. Raise it and raise SHEET_VEC4S + the WGSL MAX_RECTS in the same commit — the three are one contract.
  • STORAGE_VEC4S: derived — never edit directly.
  • The shader's morph cadence / density gate constants live in skeleton.wgsl — each is commented with units + safe range.
